title: Shared buffers, work memory and the arithmetic that sizes them

videos.script: A database server has two kinds of memory, and only one of them has a fixed size. {{two}} The first is a cache that every process shares. It is set once, when the server starts, and it holds the pages of your tables. The second belongs to each process, one operation at a time. A sort takes some. A hash takes some. An index build takes more. {{private}} You will look inside the cache and find a table that should be there and mostly is not. Then you will give the cache a quarter of the machine and watch the same query find every page. {{cache}} You will sort a million rows with too little memory and read the line that says it spilled to disk. {{spill}} And then the arithmetic: a budget for a four-gigabyte virtual machine, and one for the fifteen-gigabyte computer these recordings came from. {{budget}} The budget is the easy part. The hard part is that nothing adds up what the processes take, so the worst moment is the one to size for. {{worst}} As in the last lesson, every change is undone at the end. {{title}}
